mainTopic: Repaying a loan in front of witnesses: רב אסי, שמואל, רבא's rulings, and court cases about loans and witnesses
overview: The גמרא asks whether a borrower must repay in front of witnesses. In one version, רב אסי says yes, when the loan itself was made in front of witnesses. In רב יוסף's version, witnesses are needed only if the lender asked for them. שמואל adds that even then, the borrower is believed if he says he paid in front of two people who went overseas. A משנה seems to refute שמואל, and the גמרא defends him with a ברייתא where רבי יהודה בן בתירא agrees. רב אחא then shows that this ברייתא may be about something else. רבא's ruling is reported in two versions, and the second one follows שמואל. The גמרא then tells several court cases about loans and witnesses: a lender who named specific witnesses, a lender who was paid privately when he had asked for learned witnesses, a borrower who denied the loan entirely, and a borrower whose named witnesses denied his repayment. A new case about a 600-זוז debt begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה seems to refute רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that the משנה it just quoted is a refutation of רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב אסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. The משנה it just quoted seems to prove רב אסי wrong. This sets up רב אסי's defense in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי held that a loan made in front of witnesses must be repaid in front of witnesses. In the משנה, the borrower says 'I already gave it to you' with no witnesses, and he is believed. So it looks like repayment does not need witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; a strong challenge from a source that seems to disprove an opinion

phrases.english: A refutation of Rav Asi!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge that was raised just before this section began
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's rule that a loan made in front of witnesses must be repaid in front of witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, the borrower is believed when he says he repaid without witnesses, which contradicts the need for witnesses.

steps.title: רב אסי: my rule is only for a loan made with witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי answers that his rule applies only when the loan itself was made in front of witnesses. The משנה deals with a loan made without witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי can tell you: when I said it, I meant a case where the lender gave the loan in front of witnesses from the start, because he did not trust the borrower. Here, he did trust him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי defends himself. He says the משנה is a different case from his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lender used witnesses when giving the loan, he showed he did not trust the borrower, so the borrower must also repay in front of witnesses. In the משנה, the loan was made without witnesses. That shows trust, so the borrower is believed when he says he paid.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start; at the beginning

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רב אסי's rule depends on how the loan was made. A loan made with witnesses (no trust) must be repaid with witnesses. A loan made without witnesses (trust) does not need them.

phrases.english: Rav Asi could say to you:
When I said my rule,
it was where he lent to him in front of witnesses from the start,
since he did not trust him;
here, he did trust him.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the משנה's case, where the loan was given without witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation by narrowing רב אסי's rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (אוקימתא): the משנה deals with a loan made without witnesses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי seems to require witnesses for every repayment
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses are needed only when the loan itself was made with witnesses, which shows a lack of trust

steps.title: רב יוסף's version: witnesses are needed only if the lender asked for them
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches a different version. In it, רב אסי says even a loan made with witnesses need not be repaid with witnesses, unless the lender asked for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף teaches it this way. רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: one who lends to his friend in front of witnesses does not need to be repaid in front of witnesses. But if the lender said, 'Repay me only in front of witnesses,' the borrower must repay in front of witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב אסי's ruling, as רב יוסף taught it. This version is more lenient toward the borrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, a loan made in front of witnesses automatically needed witnesses for repayment. Here, witnesses at the loan are not enough. Only a clear request from the lender ('repay me only with witnesses') creates that need.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way; introduces a different version of the discussion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first, witnesses at the loan require witnesses at repayment. In רב יוסף's version, they do not; only the lender's explicit request does.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef teaches it like this:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Asi said:
One who lends to his friend in front of witnesses,
he does not need to repay him in front of witnesses.
But if he said: 'Do not repay me except in front of witnesses,'
he must repay him in front of witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב אסי's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loan made with witnesses does not need to be repaid with witnesses. If the lender asks for repayment in front of witnesses, the borrower must do so.

steps.title: שמואל: he can claim the witnesses went overseas
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds that even when the lender asked for witnesses, the borrower can claim he paid in front of two people who have since gone overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: when I said this before שמואל, he told me that the borrower can say, 'I repaid you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so, and they went overseas.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה reports שמואל's reaction to רב אסי's ruling. שמואל weakens the lender's request for witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the lender insisted on witnesses, the borrower is believed when he says he did use witnesses who are now unavailable. So in practice, the lender's request does not force the borrower to bring witnesses to court. This sets up the challenge from the משנה in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Before שמואל; in front of שמואל

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב יהודה, who was reporting רב אסי's ruling.

phrases.english: he said to me: He can say to him:
'I repaid you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so,
and they went off overseas.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל responds to and limits רב אסי's ruling in רב יוסף's version
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the lender asked for witnesses, the borrower is believed if he claims he repaid in front of witnesses who went overseas.

steps.title: The משנה refutes שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: when the lender said 'give it to me only in front of witnesses,' a borrower who claims 'I gave it to you' is liable. This contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: The lender said, 'I have a מנה in your hands,' and the borrower said, 'Yes.' The lender said, 'Give it to me only in front of witnesses.' The next day the lender said, 'Give it to me,' and the borrower said, 'I gave it to you.' He is liable, because he had to give it to him in front of witnesses. This is a refutation of שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a משנה and declares him refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is exactly the case of a lender who asked for witnesses. There, the borrower's simple claim 'I paid you' is not accepted. According to שמואל, he should be able to say he paid in front of witnesses who went overseas. The משנה makes him liable, which goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנה, a sum of one hundred dinars

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה shows that a lender's request for witnesses is effective: without witnesses, a claim of repayment is not believed. This looks like a refutation of שמואל. Step 6 defends him with a תנא who agrees, and in step 9 one version of רבא rules like him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a lender can protect himself by stating in advance that he will accept repayment only in front of witnesses.

phrases.english: We learned: 'I have a maneh in your hand,'
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred dinars.

phrases.english: he said to him, 'Yes';

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״אַל תִּתְּנֵהוּ לִי אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי עֵדִים״;
phrases.english: he said to him: 'Do not give it to me except in front of witnesses';
the next day he said to him, 'Give it to me,'
and he answered 'I gave it to you': he is liable,
because he needs to give it to him in front of witnesses.
A refutation of Shmuel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's view from the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that the borrower can claim he repaid before witnesses who went overseas
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, when the lender asked for witnesses, the borrower's claim 'I gave it to you' fails and he is liable. So the lender's request must be effective, against שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל follows a תנא in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that his view is a מחלוקת תנאים. In a ברייתא, the תנא קמא makes the borrower pay or prove payment, but רבי יהודה בן בתירא believes him when he says the witnesses went overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל can answer: this is a dispute between תנאים. A ברייתא says: if the lender said 'I lent to you with witnesses, repay me with witnesses,' the borrower must either pay or bring proof that he paid. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says the borrower can say: 'I repaid you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so, and they went overseas.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל from the challenge in step 5. It says שמואל holds like a different תנא who argues on that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in step 5 matches the תנא קמא of a ברייתא. שמואל is allowed to follow רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who believes the borrower's claim about the overseas witnesses. A difficulty is no longer a refutation once a תנא holds like you.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Shmuel could say to you:
It is a dispute between Tannaim,
phrases.notes: So the משנה is only one side of the argument, and שמואל follows the other side.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:
"I lent to you with witnesses,
repay me with witnesses":

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ יִתֵּן, אוֹ יָבִיא רְאָיָה שֶׁנָּתַן.
phrases.english: he must either give, or bring proof that he gave.
Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says,
he can say to him:
"I repaid you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so,
and they went overseas."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא against שמואל from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מחלוקת תנאים: שמואל follows the other side of a dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to rule out שמואל's view entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the תנא קמא of the ברייתא. שמואל follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא is talking about the time of the claim
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא argues that the ברייתא may describe a lender who spoke only when he made his claim, not at the time of the loan. If the condition was set at the time of the loan, everyone agrees the borrower must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא refutes this: how do you know the ברייתא is talking about the time of the loan? Maybe it is talking about the time of the claim, and the lender is saying: 'Didn't I lend to you with witnesses? You should have repaid me with witnesses!' But if he said it at the time of the loan, everyone agrees the borrower is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא pushes back on the defense of שמואל. He says רבי יהודה בן בתירא may not support שמואל after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's case is a lender who stated the condition when he gave the loan. רב אחא reads the ברייתא as a lender who only complained later, when he made his claim. In that case רבי יהודה בן בתירא believes the borrower. When the condition was set at the start, even רבי יהודה בן בתירא would agree the borrower must pay, so שמואל has no תנא on his side.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of the loan
At the time of the claim (in court)

steps.confusionAlert: The words of the condition are the same in both readings. The only question is WHEN the lender said them: when he gave the loan, or later when he demanded payment.

phrases.english: Rav Acha refutes:
From where do you know it is talking about the time of the loan?
Perhaps it is talking about the time of the claim,
and this is what he is saying to him:
"Didn't I lend to you with witnesses?
You should have repaid me with witnesses!"
But if he said it at the time of the loan,
all agree he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרֵיךְ רַב אַחָא: מִמַּאי דְּבִשְׁעַת הַלְוָאָה קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 6's claim that the ברייתא supports שמואל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that רבי יהודה בן בתירא agrees with שמואל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as a lender who spoke at the time of the claim, which is not שמואל's case.

steps.title: רב פפי's ruling: a loan with witnesses must be repaid with witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי, quoting רבא, rules that a loan made in front of witnesses must be repaid in front of witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: the הלכה is that someone who lends to his friend in front of witnesses must be repaid in front of witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the final הלכה. This first version comes from רב פפי, quoting רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling matches the first version of רב אסי from step 2. Witnesses at the loan are enough, even without a stated condition, to require witnesses at repayment.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lends to his fellow

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava,
the halakha is:
one who lends to his fellow with witnesses,
must be repaid with witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא, הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate to a practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A loan made with witnesses must be repaid with witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loan made with witnesses must be repaid with witnesses.

steps.title: רב פפא's version of רבא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא quotes רבא differently. Witnesses at the loan alone do not require witnesses at repayment, but a lender who asks for them gets them. Even then, a borrower who says 'I paid in front of two people who went overseas' is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: someone who lends to his friend in front of witnesses does not need to be repaid in front of witnesses. If the lender said 'Repay me only in front of witnesses,' the borrower must repay with witnesses. And if the borrower said 'I repaid you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so, and they went overseas,' he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's ruling. It argues with רב פפי's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version matches רב יוסף's version of רב אסי (step 3) and adds שמואל's rule (step 4). So in practice, a borrower who claims his witnesses went overseas is believed, even though the lender asked for witnesses. רב פפא's version supports שמואל even after רב אחא's דחיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not repay me except in front of witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבא. In רב פפי's version, witnesses at the loan mean repaying with witnesses. In רב פפא's version, only a lender who asks requires witnesses, and even then the borrower is believed if he says his witnesses went overseas (like שמואל).

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
one who lends to his fellow with witnesses
does not need to be repaid with witnesses,
and if he said "Repay me only with witnesses,"
he must be repaid with witnesses;
and if the borrower said to him:
"I repaid you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so,
and they went overseas," he is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבא's ruling that argues with step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only a lender who asks requires witnesses at repayment. Even then, the borrower is believed if he says his witnesses went overseas.

steps.title: Memory aid for the stories that follow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a string of key words that will help the learner remember the upcoming stories about loans and witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory aid: ראובן and שמעון, who learned הלכה; borrowed and repaid; so-and-so and so-and-so; gallnuts on the side; trusted like two.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא lists short key words, one for each of the stories it is about to tell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is a hook for a story coming next, so it will only make sense after you learn those stories. No הלכה is being decided here.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid listing key words
Gallnuts (used to make ink and for tanning)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to read the סימן as one sentence that makes sense on its own. Each phrase belongs to a different story that comes next.

phrases.english: A mnemonic:
Reuven and Shimon, who learned halakha,
borrowed and repaid,
so-and-so and so-and-so,
gallnuts on the side,
with trust like two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ruling to a set of stories, starting with a memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is a memory aid that sets up the coming stories.

steps.title: A lender names specific witnesses for repayment
steps.stepSummary: A lender told the borrower to repay in front of ראובן and שמעון, but the borrower repaid in front of two other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who told his friend: "When you pay me back, pay me back in front of ראובן and שמעון." The borrower went and paid him back in front of two other people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case and sets up the question that the next steps will answer: does this repayment count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9 we learned that a lender who asks for witnesses at repayment gets them. Here the lender went further and named two specific people. The borrower did use witnesses, just not the ones the lender named.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain person; the usual way the גמרא opens a story
In front of; in the presence of
Literally 'from the world'; ordinary people, not the ones that were named

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his fellow:
"When you repay me,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some have the words in square brackets. Both mean 'when you pay me back.'

phrases.english: repay me in front of Reuven and Shimon."
He went and repaid him in front of two other people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the first story from the סימן given in Step 10. It applies Step 9's rule that a lender who asks for witnesses gets them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: the lender named specific witnesses, and the borrower repaid in front of different witnesses.

steps.title: אביי: any two witnesses are enough
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the repayment counts, because the real point was to have two witnesses, and there were two.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He told him to pay in front of two people, and he paid him in front of two people.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his ruling on the story: the borrower kept the condition well enough, so the debt is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads the names ראובן and שמעון as just an example of 'two witnesses.' Since the borrower did pay in front of two witnesses, the lender's real goal was met.

keyTerms.meaning: Two people; a pair of witnesses

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He told him "in front of two,"
and he repaid him in front of two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling on the case set up in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Naming specific witnesses only means 'two witnesses,' so repaying in front of any two is valid.

steps.title: רבא: the named witnesses matter
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's view. The lender named specific people on purpose, so that the borrower could not brush him off by pointing to other witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: That is exactly why he told him "in front of ראובן and שמעון": so that the borrower could not push him off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues against אביי and says the names were not just an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lender only wanted 'two witnesses,' he would have just said so. He named ראובן and שמעון on purpose, so that the borrower could not brush him off by pointing to other witnesses the lender cannot check. So paying in front of other people does not keep the condition.

keyTerms.meaning: For this reason; that is exactly why
Push him off; brush him aside

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is against using witnesses in general. He agrees there were two witnesses. His point is only that the lender asked for these two specific people.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
That is why he told him "in front of Reuven and Shimon":
so that he could not push him off!
phrases.notes: He means the borrower should not be able to brush off the lender by naming some other witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: לְהָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's ruling in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects אביי's reading of the lender's condition.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי treats the specific names as meaningless. In fact, the lender named them on purpose, so that the borrower could not escape by pointing to other witnesses.

steps.title: A lender asks for learned witnesses, but is paid privately
steps.stepSummary: A lender asked to be repaid in front of two people who learned הלכה. The borrower paid him privately, and the coins were then lost through an accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who told his friend: "When you pay me back, pay me back in front of two people who have learned הלכה." The borrower went and paid him privately, just between the two of them. Then those coins were lost through an accident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story and sets up a court case that רב נחמן will decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the borrower did not use any witnesses at all, and the lender accepted the money. The coins were then lost through an אונס, something outside the lender's control. Now we need to know who bears the loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Who have learned הלכה; Torah scholars
Literally 'between his and his'; privately, with no witnesses
Were lost through an אונס, an accident nobody could prevent

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his fellow:
"When you repay me, repay me
in front of two people who have learned halacha."
He went and repaid him privately, just between them.
Those coins were lost through an accident.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְחַבְרֵיהּ: כִּי פָּרְעַתְּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the next story from the סימן in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: the condition asked for learned witnesses, the payment was made privately, and the money was then lost.

steps.title: The lender claims he held the money only as a deposit
steps.stepSummary: Before רב נחמן, the lender admits he received the money. He argues that he took it only as a deposit until learned witnesses could be found, so the lost money was not repayment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lender came before רב נחמן and said: "Yes, I did receive the money from him, but only as a deposit. I told myself: let it stay with me as a deposit until two people who learned הלכה happen to come, and then he will keep his condition."
steps.whatsHappening: The lender makes his argument in court for why the borrower still owes him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender admits he took the money but changes what it was: a פקדון, not a payment. Someone who holds a deposit for free is not responsible when it is lost through an accident. If he is right, the loss falls on the borrower, and the loan is still unpaid.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit; something you hold for someone else
That they happen to come along

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: He came before Rav Nachman and said to him:
"Yes, I did receive them from him,
but as a deposit;
and I said: let it be with me as a deposit

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּמִתְרְמוּ בֵּי תְרֵי דְּתָנוּ הִלְכְתָא
phrases.english: until two people who learned halacha happen to come
and he fulfills his condition."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The lender presents his side of the case from Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender's claim: money received without the required witnesses was held as a deposit, not as repayment.

steps.title: רב נחמן: taking the money is full repayment
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that since the lender admits he took the money, it was a valid repayment. If the lender still wants the condition kept, he can bring the money, and it will be repaid in front of רב נחמן and רב ששת, who are learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: "Since you admit you really took the money from him, it is a proper repayment. If you say he still has to keep his condition, go bring the money. רב ששת and I have learned הלכה, ספרא, ספרי, תוספתא, and the whole תלמוד."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rejects the lender's argument and rules that the debt was paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition about witnesses was only for the lender's protection, so he could prove he was paid. Since the lender himself admits he got the money, no proof is needed, and it counts as payment. The loss is therefore the lender's. רב נחמן's sharp line shows that insisting on the condition now is pointless: two learned people are right here.

keyTerms.meaning: Collections of early teachings of the תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: A condition to repay in front of witnesses is there to protect the lender. If the lender admits he received the money, it counts as repayment even without those witnesses.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that witness conditions in loans are about proof, not about whether the payment really happened. This connects back to the debate in Steps 8–9 about witnesses at repayment.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since you admit
that you certainly took them from him,
it is a proper repayment;
if you say he must fulfill his condition,
go bring them.
phrases.notes: He means: bring the money, and the borrower will hand it to you again right here in front of us.

phrases.english: For here are I and Rav Sheshet,
who have learned halacha, Sifra, and Sifrei,
and Tosefta, and the whole Talmud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּקָא מוֹדֵית דְּוַדַּאי שְׁקַלְתִּינְהוּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the lender's deposit claim from Step 15 and rules on the case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once the lender admits he received the money, it is a full repayment despite the unmet witness condition. The loss is the lender's.

steps.title: A borrower denies the loan, but witnesses say it was lent and repaid
steps.stepSummary: A lender demands 100 זוזים. The borrower says there was never any loan. The lender brings witnesses who say there was a loan and that it was repaid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man said to another: 'Give me the hundred זוזים I lent you.' The other said: 'This never happened.' The lender went and brought witnesses, and they said he lent him the money and the borrower repaid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new court case. The next two steps are two opinions on how to rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something strange happens here. The borrower says 'there was never a loan.' The lender's own witnesses back up the loan, but they also say it was repaid. So the borrower's claim does not match the witnesses at all.

keyTerms.meaning: These things never happened (a full denial)

steps.confusionAlert: The witnesses are brought by the lender, yet they also say the money was paid back. Their testimony helps the borrower and hurts the borrower at the same time, and that is what makes the case hard.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his fellow:
"Give me the hundred zuz that I lent you."
He said to him: "These things never happened."
He went and brought witnesses
who said that he lent him and that he repaid him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְחַבְרֵיהּ: ״הַב לִי מְאָה זוּזֵי דְּאוֹזֵיפְתָּךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new lending case after the case of רב נחמן and the learned witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the facts: the borrower fully denies the loan, and the witnesses say there was a loan and that it was repaid.

steps.title: אביי: the same witnesses said both things, so nothing can be done
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the court cannot make the borrower pay. The same witnesses who told us about the loan also told us it was repaid.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What can we do? The witnesses say he lent him, and the same witnesses say he repaid him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his ruling: the borrower does not have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only proof that a loan ever existed comes from these witnesses. They also say it was paid back. We cannot accept half of their testimony and ignore the other half, so the borrower is free.

phrases.english: אביי said: What can we do?
They say that he lent him,
and they say that he repaid him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first ruling on the case from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The borrower does not have to pay, because the same witnesses who prove the loan also prove the repayment.

steps.title: רבא: saying 'I never borrowed' is like saying 'I never repaid'
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי. By saying he never borrowed, the borrower is in effect admitting he never paid. Once the loan is proven, he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Anyone who says 'I did not borrow' is treated like someone who says 'I did not repay.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite ruling: the borrower has to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there was never a loan, as the borrower claims, then he never paid anything back either. So his own words cancel out the part of the testimony that says he repaid. What remains is the witnesses' proof of the loan, together with his own admission that he did not repay.

keyTerms.meaning: Is considered like / is equal to

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: the same witnesses said 'lent' and 'repaid,' so the borrower is free. רבא: a person who denies the loan has in effect said he never repaid, so he must pay.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule: a borrower who falsely denies the whole loan loses the chance to claim later, or through witnesses, that he paid it back.

phrases.english: רבא said: Anyone who says "I did not borrow"
is considered like one who says "I did not repay."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite ruling to אביי's in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who denies the loan has in effect said he never repaid it. Once witnesses prove the loan, he must pay.

steps.title: The borrower names witnesses to his repayment, and they deny it
steps.stepSummary: A lender demands 100 זוזים. The borrower says he paid in front of two named people. Those two come and say it never happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man said to another: 'Give me the hundred זוזים I claim from you.' The other said: 'Didn't I pay you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so?' Those two people came and said: 'This never happened.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second court case. The next steps discuss how to treat the borrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the borrower admits there was a loan and says he paid it back. He even names the people who saw him pay. Those very people say they never saw it, so his story seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: That I claim from you (that you owe me)

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his fellow:
"Give me the hundred zuz that I claim from you."

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״לֹא פְּרַעְתִּיךָ בִּפְנֵי פְּלוֹנִי וּפְלוֹנִי?״
phrases.english: He said to him: "Didn't I repay you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so?"
So-and-so and so-and-so came and said:
"These things never happened."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְחַבְרֵיהּ: ״הַב לִי מְאָה זוּזֵי דְּמַסֵּיקְנָא בָּךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case after the dispute between אביי and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the facts: the people the borrower named as witnesses to his repayment deny that it ever happened.

steps.title: רב ששת first thinks the borrower is now a known denier
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת's first thought is that the borrower has been shown to be a כפרן. His claim that he repaid would then no longer be believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת thought to say: He is now established as a denier.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת offers a first idea for the ruling. The next step will push back on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His own named witnesses contradicted him, so it looks like he lied. A person shown to be a כפרן is not believed when he says 'I paid,' so he would have to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say (a first idea that may be rejected)
He is established as a denier (a person who falsely denies his debts)

phrases.english: רב ששת thought to say:
He is established as a denier,

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְמֵימַר: הוּחְזַק כַּפְרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first ruling on the case from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת's first thought, rejected in the next step: because his own named witnesses contradicted him, the borrower is treated as a כפרן and is not believed that he repaid.

steps.title: רבא: people do not remember what was not their responsibility
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב ששת's idea. The named people had no responsibility in the matter, so they may simply not remember it. Their denial does not make the borrower a כפרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Any matter that is not a person's responsibility does not stay on his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב ששת and explains why the borrower is not treated as a liar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A repayment between two other people is not something an onlooker has any reason to remember. So when they say 'it never happened,' it may only mean they forgot. It does not show that the borrower lied.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not placed upon him (not his responsibility)
Is not on his mind (he does not remember it)

steps.whatToRemember: Being contradicted by people who had no reason to pay attention does not make someone a כפרן, because they may simply have forgotten.

phrases.english: רבא said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מִילְּתָא דְלָא רַמְיָא עֲלֵיהּ דְּאִינָשׁ
phrases.english: Any matter that is not a person's responsibility
is not on his mind.
phrases.notes: He means people easily forget things that were not their concern.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: כֹּל מִילְּתָא דְלָא רַמְיָא עֲלֵיהּ דְּאִינָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's idea from step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects treating the borrower as a כפרן because his named witnesses denied the repayment.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב ששת's idea assumes the witnesses' denial proves the borrower lied. They may simply have forgotten something that was not their concern.

steps.title: A third case begins: a claim of 600 זוזים and a repayment in produce
steps.stepSummary: A lender demands 600 זוזים. The borrower begins to answer that he already paid with a hundred קבין of something. The case continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man said to another: 'Give me the six hundred זוזים I claim from you.' The other said: 'But didn't I repay you a hundred קבין...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a third court case, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the borrower says he paid in goods measured in קבין, not in coins. The rest of his claim and the ruling come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: קב measures (a unit of volume for produce)

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his fellow:

phrases.aramaic: ״הַב לִי שֵׁית מְאָה זוּזֵי דְּמַסֵּיקְנָא בָּךְ״.
phrases.english: "Give me the six hundred zuz that I claim from you."
He said to him: "But didn't I repay you a hundred kav
phrases.notes: His sentence keeps going on the next amud, which tells us what the hundred קב were of.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְחַבְרֵיהּ: ״הַב לִי שֵׁית מְאָה זוּזֵי דְּמַסֵּיקְנָא בָּךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case after רבא's answer to רב ששת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the facts: the borrower claims he repaid part of a 600-זוז debt in goods measured in קבין. The case is not finished here.
